At the one-day horizon, I estimated 742.5, essentially expecting very little movement from the current level, consistent with mean-reversion tendencies in most financial or commodity markets over short windows. At one week, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 745, reflecting a mild positive drift assumption while acknowledging that short-term momentum or fundamental catalysts could sustain a gentle upward bias. At one month, I moved to 750, incorporating a longer-run drift that might reflect underlying growth trends, inflation adjustments, or structural demand factors depending on the asset in question — though the direction assumption here is relatively modest and not strongly conviction-driven.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which follows standard uncertainty scaling. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 31 points (727–758), reflecting the relatively constrained volatility typical of a single trading session. At one week, the interval widens to 60 points (715–775), capturing the accumulation of daily price variance across five or more sessions. At one month, the interval reaches 110 points (695–805), reflecting not just compounded daily volatility but also the greater probability of regime shifts, macro surprises, or sentiment changes over a longer period. The widths were also influenced by my uncertainty about the specific asset class, since without knowing whether this is an equity index, commodity, currency pair, or something else, I had to assume moderate volatility parameters.

There are several risks that could push outcomes well outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a major positive catalyst — such as a surprise policy announcement, strong earnings or economic data, or a short squeeze — could drive prices sharply above 758 within a day or above 805 within a month. On the downside, geopolitical shocks, liquidity crises, unexpected regulatory actions, or a broader risk-off episode could push the price below 727 in the near term or below 695 over a month. These tail scenarios are by construction excluded from a 90% confidence interval, meaning there is roughly a 10% cumulative probability I assigned to outcomes outside the stated ranges.
